name: _sparse_csc_tensor_unsafe
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_csc_tensor_unsafe(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::_sparse_csc_tensor_unsafe(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract - registered overloads, keyword arguments, returns, error behavior, aliasing and mutation - and must not be narrowed to this one signature. Semantics from the tests: this is the unchecked CSC constructor. It returns a sparse CSC tensor that stores the caller's ccol_indices, row_indices and values buffers by alias (same storage, shape, stride, offset; writes through the components are visible in the inputs), performs no metadata or buffer-length validation, creates no autograd edge (the tests assert only that `res_out.requires_grad` is False and that `res_out.grad_fn is ref_out.grad_fn is None`), and has no broadcast operands. `size` is the full logical size list and is the reported result shape (the tests assert `tuple(res_out.shape) == tuple(ref_out.shape) == tuple(size)`): the trailing (rows, cols) entries address the matrix and the leading entries are the batch axes the tests build, with `values` shaped as batch + [nnz]; the dense dimension is exercised only by the unchecked 2-D `values` case (values shape [2, 1] with size [3, 2]), and `sparse_dim()`, `dense_dim()` and `nnz` are compared against the ATen reference rather than to fixed constants; rank-0/rank-1 size lists are accepted and keep the requested shape with empty components. The three buffer parameters are Tensor and `size` is List[int]; dtype, layout, device and pin_memory are keyword-only options. The ATen Optional defaults are non-JSON `None` sentinels and are retained here as JSON null; the tests evidence the effective omitted-argument defaults (dtype float32, layout sparse_csc, device cpu, pin_memory absent) rather than any single benchmark tuple. The constructor does validate option compatibility - mismatched values dtype, foreign layouts, non-list size, unknown device, missing device on accelerators, cross-device buffers and `pin_memory=True` on a non-CPU device all raise RuntimeError/TypeError/ValueError/NotImplementedError - and those error paths, plus the malformed-metadata comparisons and omitted-keyword forms, remain owned by pytest.
